chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever walks in one shoe, a touch of Satan strikes him, and it does not leave him except what Allah wills.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of walking in one shoe according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the spiritual vulnerability associated with asymmetry in daily attire, linking the physical act of wearing a single shoe to 'mass' (a touch or affliction) by Satan. Scholars interpret this not merely as a superstition but as a sign of spiritual negligence, where the disruption of natural order invites minor demonic influence or distraction from worship, unless preserved by Allah's will.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who walks in one shoe, so a touch of the Satan<sup>la</sup> hits him, it would not leave him (the injury) except what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one walks with one shoe and if a touch of Satan reaches, him it will not leave him unless Allah wants otherwise.’”
